title: Mr. Kitayuta, the Treasure Hunter
statementMd:
The Shuseki Islands are an archipelago of $30001$ small islands in the Yutampo Sea. The islands are evenly spaced along a line, numbered from $0$ to $30000$ from the west to the east. These islands are known to contain many treasures. There are $*n*$ gems in the Shuseki Islands in total, and the $*i*$-th gem is located on island $*p*_{*i*}$.

Mr. Kitayuta has just arrived at island $0$. With his great jumping ability, he will repeatedly perform jumps between islands to the east according to the following process:

- First, he will jump from island $0$ to island $*d*$.
- After that, he will continue jumping according to the following rule. Let $*l*$ be the length of the previous jump, that is, if his previous jump was from island $*prev*$ to island $*cur*$, let $*l* = *cur* - *prev*$. He will perform a jump of length $*l* - 1$, $*l*$ or $*l* + 1$ to the east. That is, he will jump to island $(*cur* + *l* - 1)$, $(*cur* + *l*)$ or $(*cur* + *l* + 1)$ (if they exist). The length of a jump must be positive, that is, he cannot perform a jump of length $0$ when $*l* = 1$. If there is no valid destination, he will stop jumping.

Mr. Kitayuta will collect the gems on the islands visited during the process. Find the maximum number of gems that he can collect.

## Input

The first line of the input contains two space-separated integers $*n*$ and $*d*$ ($1 ≤ *n*, *d* ≤ 30000$), denoting the number of the gems in the Shuseki Islands and the length of the Mr. Kitayuta's first jump, respectively.

The next $*n*$ lines describe the location of the gems. The $*i*$-th of them ($1 ≤ *i* ≤ *n*$) contains a integer $*p*_{*i*}$ ($*d* ≤ *p*_{1} ≤ *p*_{2} ≤ ... ≤ *p*_{*n*} ≤ 30000$), denoting the number of the island that contains the $*i*$-th gem.

## Output

Print the maximum number of gems that Mr. Kitayuta can collect.

## Note

In the first sample, the optimal route is 0 $→$ 10 (+1 gem) $→$ 19 $→$ 27 (+2 gems) $→ ...$

In the second sample, the optimal route is 0 $→$ 8 $→$ 15 $→$ 21$→$ 28 (+1 gem) $→$ 36 (+1 gem) $→$ 45 (+1 gem) $→$ 55 (+1 gem) $→$ 66 (+1 gem) $→$ 78 (+1 gem) $→ ...$

In the third sample, the optimal route is 0 $→$ 7 $→$ 13 $→$ 18 (+1 gem) $→$ 24 (+2 gems) $→$ 30 (+1 gem) $→ ...$
statementZhMd:
修积群岛是位于尤坦波海的一片群岛，由 $30001$ 个小岛组成。这些岛屿沿一条直线等间距排列，从西到东编号为 $0$ 到 $30000$。众所周知，这些岛上藏有许多宝藏。修积群岛上一共有 $*n*$ 颗宝石，第 $*i*$ 颗宝石位于岛屿 $*p*_{*i*}$ 上。

北爷刚刚抵达岛屿 $0$。凭借出色的跳跃能力，他将按照以下过程不断向东在岛屿之间跳跃：

- 首先，他会从岛屿 $0$ 跳到岛屿 $*d*$。
- 之后，他将按照以下规则继续跳跃。设上一次跳跃的长度为 $*l*$，也就是说，如果他上一次是从岛屿 $*prev*$ 跳到岛屿 $*cur*$，则 $*l* = *cur* - *prev*$。他会向东跳跃 $*l* - 1$、$*l*$ 或 $*l* + 1$ 的距离。也就是说，他会跳到岛屿 $(*cur* + *l* - 1)$、$(*cur* + *l*)$ 或 $(*cur* + *l* + 1)$（如果这些岛屿存在）。跳跃的长度必须为正，因此当 $*l* = 1$ 时，他不能进行长度为 $0$ 的跳跃。如果不存在合法的目的地，他将停止跳跃。

北爷会收集跳跃过程中访问过的岛屿上的宝石。请计算他最多能收集多少颗宝石。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含两个用空格分隔的整数 $*n*$ 和 $*d*$（$1 ≤ *n*, *d* ≤ 30000$），分别表示修积群岛上的宝石数量以及北爷第一次跳跃的长度。

接下来的 $*n*$ 行描述宝石的位置。其中第 $*i*$ 行（$1 ≤ *i* ≤ *n*$）包含一个整数 $*p*_{*i*}$（$*d* ≤ *p*_{1} ≤ *p*_{2} ≤ ... ≤ *p*_{*n*} ≤ 30000$），表示第 $*i*$ 颗宝石所在岛屿的编号。

## 输出格式

输出北爷最多能够收集的宝石数量。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，最优路线为 0 $→$ 10（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 19 $→$ 27（+2 颗宝石）$→ ...$

在第二个样例中，最优路线为 0 $→$ 8 $→$ 15 $→$ 21$→$ 28（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 36（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 45（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 55（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 66（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 78（+1 颗宝石）$→ ...$

在第三个样例中，最优路线为 0 $→$ 7 $→$ 13 $→$ 18（+1 颗宝石）$→$ 24（+2 颗宝石）$→$ 30（+1 颗宝石）$→ ...$
